meta.lesson: L2 — Prompt Safety, Injection Awareness and Guardrails
meta.title: Risk and controls document before building: Part B

safety.student_notice: Don't include personal or identifying information in your answers.
safety.scope_guard: Description level only, and every injection example entirely fictional and marked as such. No real document, employee or customer data, contract, medical or financial information, or real identifying detail goes into any AI tool, not even to test a scenario. If a participant pastes something that looks real, the coach tells them to replace it with a description.
never_soften: Completing this document does not mean the system is secure. It is an initial risk-identification stage, not a warranty.
The guardrails defined here are a starting point, reviewed again during the build stages. Defining them is not a promise that they are sufficient.
safety.no_attack_help: The coach never helps write, improve or complete an injection payload and never suggests a phrasing that would work on a real system. If the participant drifts into attack technique, it names the boundary and turns them back to the guardrail.

checks: names the business problem
names the architecture from Module 1
states the Build vs Buy decision
two or three sentences, and their own case rather than the HR demo
t1_case_reminder.common_miss: Describes the tool but not the problem it solves, or leaves out Build vs Buy entirely.

checks: three scenarios
at least one direct
at least one indirect, tied to a real channel in their architecture
each scenario says direct or indirect, and whether it is also sensitive information disclosure and/or excessive agency
every example is fictional and marked as such
t2_scenarios.common_miss: Three variations on a user typing something malicious, with no document, email, CRM note or uploaded file, or excessive agency used as a catch-all for a scenario with no action and no tool.

checks: names guardrails from the seven by name
covers every scenario in section 2
says why that guardrail stops that specific problem
does not stop at one guardrail for everything
t3_guardrails.common_miss: A generic control such as instructing the system to be careful, which is not a guardrail because nothing about it can be checked.

checks: a list of concrete actions, not principles
includes an action with an external or irreversible effect, of the kind of sending an external email, updating a record or a financial decision
draws the boundary between drafting and executing
t4_approvals.common_miss: States that a human is in the loop without naming a single action that stops for approval.

checks: an entry per scenario
says who is alerted
says at which stage, with logging first and repetition handled
role titles only, no real names
the target has the authority to act
t5_escalation.common_miss: One destination with no stages, or escalation to a named individual, or to a role with no authority over the problem.

checks: names the stakeholders relevant to their own case, from the seven
at least one concrete question per stakeholder
the questions are ones they cannot answer alone
t6_stakeholders.common_miss: A list of roles with no questions, or a question the participant has already answered for themselves.

checks: all five answered yes or no
an honest no where the work is not done
the two 3A.1 answers, data classification and stakeholders, reflect Lesson 1 outputs that actually exist
t7_readiness.common_miss: Five yes answers over thin sections above, which records nothing and hides the open work the build module will look for.

outcome_logic.when: section 2 has fewer than three scenarios
outcome_logic.path: Add scenarios until there are three. Start from the sources in your own architecture rather than from a blank page.
Add an indirect one. Walk the four channels and pick the one your architecture actually has: a policy document, an incoming email or service request, a CRM free-text field, or a file a user uploads.
Add a direct one: a user typing the bypass attempt into the conversation, so the human actor is identified.

outcome_logic.when: section 2 classifies channel but never sensitive information disclosure or excessive agency
outcome_logic.path: Complete the classification. For each scenario say whether it is also sensitive information disclosure, or excessive agency, or both. If injection succeeds it usually becomes disclosure.

outcome_logic.when: excessive agency is claimed for a scenario with no action and no tool
outcome_logic.path: Excessive agency is about what the system can actually do. If nothing is sent, updated or invoked, reclassify it and keep excessive agency for the scenario where the system acts.

outcome_logic.when: section 3 is generic, or names fewer than two of the seven guardrails
outcome_logic.path: Replace the general statement with named guardrails from the seven, and for each one write the sentence saying what it blocks in that specific scenario.

outcome_logic.when: section 4 lists no action with an external or irreversible effect
outcome_logic.path: Name the actions that stop for a person: sending an external email, updating a record, a financial decision. Drafting is allowed; executing is what needs approval.
Give the escalation stages, not just a destination: automatic logging first, then the business owner with the context, then Security and the DPO on repetition.

outcome_logic.when: section 5 names no role, or looks like a personal name
outcome_logic.path: Write role titles only, and check that the role you escalate to is actually authorized to handle the problem.

outcome_logic.when: section 6 has no question mark, or fewer than two stakeholders
outcome_logic.path: Give each relevant stakeholder one concrete question, of the kind on the stakeholder table, and keep the questions to things you must not decide alone.
Answer all five, yes or no. A no is a result: it tells the build module what is still open.

outcome_logic.when: the readiness checklist is all yes while sections 3, 4 or 5 are thin
outcome_logic.path: Re-read what you wrote above before you tick yes. The checklist records the work; it does not replace it.
Go back to Lesson 1 and finish the four-level classification for your sources. Section 2 cannot say what must not be exposed until that exists.
Go back to your Lesson 1 stakeholder map and mark which of the roles your own case touches, then bring them into section 6.

Save it as one document with a clear name and keep it to hand. It is the entry condition to the build modules, and it is checked at the start of the module. Two things it does not do: it does not make the system secure, and it does not settle the guardrails, which are reviewed again while you build.
